similar_scenes.name: Hardcore en la era del punk-pop: emocore, ska-core y post-hardcore
similar_scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
similar_scenes.desc: Mientras las revistas anuncian la «muerte del punk», el hardcore se convierte en un movimiento que no deja pueblo sin tocar y genera subgéneros. El «emocore» (Jawbreaker, Weezer, Sunny Day Real Estate, Promise Ring, At The Drive-In, Jimmy Eat World, Seaweed); el hardcore progresivo de Washington (Nation Of Ulysses, Make-Up, Shudder To Think, Jawbox, Edsel, Lungfish, Circus Lupus, Dismemberment Plan); el «ska-core» (Operation Ivy, Rancid, Mighty Mighty Bosstones, Sublime, No Doubt); el punk-pop que llega a las listas (Green Day, Offspring, Flop, Pennywise, Pegboy, Superchunk, Queers); el garage-punk californiano (Drive Like Jehu, Rocket From The Crypt, Blink 182, Zen Guerrilla); el jazzcore (Bazooka, Iceburn); la vieja escuela (D Generation, Supersuckers, Zeke, Dropkick Murphys, Silverfish, Turbonegro) y el post-hardcore de Unwound.
similar_scenes.family: Punk, new wave, hardcore y noise

podcast.title: Big Black's Atomizer - A Groundbreaking Album
podcast.body: Big Black's debut album, *Atomizer*, produced by Steve Albini, was recognized as a groundbreaking post-hardcore record. It innovatively replaced conventional drums with a Roland TR-606 drum machine, creating a distinct industrial sound that garnered critical acclaim. "un avisonador aposjarco en la cual prescinde de la batería convencional a favor de una caja de ritmo Roland T. R. 606, la cual aporta un sonido más industrial."

srcs.episode: 7 discos para entender la producción de STEVE ALBINI

podcast.title: Crossover with Third Wave Emo
podcast.body: During the third wave of emo, there was a significant crossover and fragmentation, with many bands being classified as post-hardcore alongside emo, punk, pop punk, and metalcore. "There was, in short, a crossover between proper emo, if you'll allow me to use that term, an emo-like bands, who were probably best classified as punk, pop punk, post-hardcore, and metalcore."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Definition
podcast.body: "Post-hardcore" refers to a band with a sound that could not have existed had it not been preceded and influenced by hardcore punk. The DNA of the sound is similar but has evolved. "Same thing in the case of post hardcore. It's a band with a sound that could have not existed, had it not been preceded, and influenced by hardcore punk."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Definition
podcast.body: Post-hardcore is a derivative of hardcore punk, characterized by a greater emphasis on melody and experimentation with song structure. "Post-hardcore is hardcore punk, but with more emphasis on melody and experimentation with song structure."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What Exactly is Post Rock? Part 2

podcast.title: Developed from Hardcore Punk
podcast.body: Post-hardcore is listed as one of the genres whose development was fundamentally influenced by hardcore punk. "el post hardcore."

srcs.episode: Egg Punk: Explorando el lado más raro del punk

podcast.title: Early 90s Mention
podcast.body: Post-hardcore was mentioned as one of the many forms of Alt Rock that enjoyed moments in the sun during the 90s, showcasing the heavier and more aggressive end of the alternative spectrum. "We could have just as well mentioned, early emo, dream pop, math rock, post-hardcore, alt metal, alt country, Tweet Rock, contemporary Christian alternative music, and so many more."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Evolution from Hardcore
podcast.body: Post-hardcore was identified as a progression from hardcore in the lineage of aggressive music that Alexis on Fire explored and contributed to, eventually leading into screamo. "You have punk, which turns into hardcore, which turns into post-hardcore, which becomes screamo and all that sort of weirdness, right?"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Alexisonfire - In Their Own Words Podcast

podcast.title: Hardcore Influence
podcast.body: Post-hardcore is listed as one of the genres that has been significantly influenced by hardcore music since the 1980s. "we've seen the influence this music has had on metal and in creating post-hardcore music as well as skate punk and emo."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Origins in Hardcore/Metal Fusion
podcast.body: Post-hardcore emerged from the blend of hardcore and metal, as exemplified by bands like NoMeansNo. The sound of NoMeansNo is noted for containing elements that would later define the post-hardcore genre, influencing a generation of bands. "If you listen carefully to what they did, you can hear elements of what would become known as post-hardcore, a sound that would later birth groups like at the drive-in, Rollins Band, Alexis on Fire, Billy Talent, The Death Tones and Silverstein."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
